excerpt: Glass-walled conference rooms and demountable partitions add a distinct line to US janitorial bills, priced per visit, per panel, per square foot of glass, or per hour. This guide gives national ranges, minimums, and the math to check any proposal.
quickAnswer: Nationally, routine interior glass and partition spot-cleaning is usually added to janitorial contracts at $15–$35 per visit, while full both-sides detail cleaning prices at $3–$8 per standard panel or $0.15–$0.40 per sq ft of glass surface. Hourly billing runs $35–$65 for standard work and $55–$95 for glass above 10 feet requiring lifts, with project minimums of $150–$300.

blocks.text: Interior glass shows up in nearly every office built or renovated since 2015: frameless conference room walls, glass office fronts, sidelights beside doors, demountable partition systems, and glass railings at stairs. Fingerprints at handle height and smudges where people lean appear daily, while dust and film build up across the full panel over weeks. Vendors separate these two needs into a routine add-on and a periodic detail clean, and they price them differently.

items: Per visit add-on: a flat charge on top of the routine janitorial rate for spot-cleaning glass doors, sidelights, and conference partitions at touch height.
Per panel: used for detail cleaning of standard partition modules, typically 3–5 ft wide and 8–9 ft tall, both sides.
Per square foot of glass: used for large or irregular glass walls, measured as one side of glass surface; both-sides cleaning is sometimes counted as double.
Per hour: used for high glass, atriums, or mixed tasks where measurement is impractical.

blocks.title: Production-rate check
blocks.text: A trained technician with a squeegee and microfiber typically details 20–30 standard panels, both sides, per hour at normal height. At $35–$65 per hour that implies about $1.20–$3.25 per panel in labor, and vendors then add overhead, travel, and supplies to reach the $3–$8 range.
Worked Example: 18,000 Sq Ft Office With Glass Conference Wing

Picture a tech company floor with eight glass conference rooms averaging five 4x9 ft panels each (40 panels), twelve glass-fronted private offices with two panels each (24 panels), and 16 glass doors and sidelights. On routine service five nights a week, a $25 per visit glass add-on equals $25 times 21.65 visits, or about $541 per month. A monthly full detail of 64 panels at $5.00 each adds $320 per month. The combined glass line is roughly $861 per month, about $0.048 per sq ft of floor area per month. If the vendor instead quoted per sq ft of glass, 64 panels times 36 sq ft is 2,304 sq ft; at $0.20 per sq ft one side, both sides would run $922 per detail, so the per-panel bid is the better value for this layout.
What Drives Glass Prices Up or Down

items: Height: anything above 10 ft moves to specialty hourly rates and may require a scissor lift and operator training under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.67 and ANSI A92 standards.
Frosting and decals: privacy film and manifestation strips must be cleaned gently with non-ammonia solution, slowing work.
Access: occupied conference rooms with whiteboards, monitors, and furniture against glass reduce production.
Frequency: weekly detail pricing per panel is usually 20–30% lower than quarterly because film never builds up.
Hardware: patch fittings, door rails, and tracks on demountable systems need separate wipe-down and are often excluded unless named.

blocks.text: Most streaking comes from chemical residue, not technique. Require a non-ammonia, low-residue glass cleaner at the manufacturer's dilution, dispensed from labeled bottles. Heavy-duty chemical-resistant sprayers like the Impact 32-oz bottles with Viton seals, graduated measurement markings, and color coding help crews keep glass cleaner separate from disinfectants and meet OSHA HazCom secondary-container labeling. Conference rooms with glass walls usually have upholstered chairs and carpet too; vendors that bundle glass detail with seat and carpet spotting may use a compact heated extractor such as the Hoover Commercial Spotter CH84000, with a 1.2-gallon tank, stainless upholstery tool, and 13 lb weight, or a larger dual-motor unit like the Bissell BigGreen BG10 with a 10.5-inch path for conference room carpet. Bundling these tasks into one detail visit lets the minimum apply once.
How to Write the Glass Scope

items.name: Inventory the glass
items.text: Count panels, doors, and sidelights by room and note any glass above 10 ft.

items.name: Separate routine and detail
items.text: Define nightly or weekly touch-height spot cleaning separately from full-height both-sides detail on a monthly or quarterly calendar.

items.name: Name inclusions
items.text: State whether frames, tracks, door hardware, and privacy film are included.

items.name: Set a quality standard
items.text: Specify no streaks visible at 3 ft under normal lighting, and allow a reclean at no cost within 24 hours.

items.name: Require insurance and lift credentials
items.text: Obtain a certificate of insurance and, for high glass, proof of aerial lift training.

blocks.title: Daytime porter coverage for glass-heavy floors
blocks.text: If executives or clients notice fingerprints by midday, a day porter wiping glass doors at lunch often costs less than increasing night detail frequency, especially when the porter is already on site for restroom checks.

faqs.q: Is interior glass cleaning included in standard office cleaning?
faqs.a: Spot-cleaning glass entry doors is commonly included, but conference partitions, office fronts, and full-height detail usually are not. Many vendors list interior glass as a $15–$35 per visit add-on. Confirm the height limit and which panels are covered in the written scope.

faqs.q: How do I convert a per-visit glass add-on to a monthly cost?
faqs.a: Multiply the per-visit price by visits per month. Weekly service is 4.333 visits per month, twice weekly 8.66, and five nights a week about 21.65. A $25 add-on on twice-weekly service is roughly $217 per month.

faqs.q: Are there safety rules for cleaning tall interior glass?
faqs.a: Yes. Ladder use falls under OSHA walking-working surface rules, and aerial lifts require trained operators under OSHA and ANSI A92 standards. Vendors should carry general liability coverage, typically $1 million per occurrence, and provide a certificate of insurance before high-glass work.

faqs.q: Which cleaning chemicals are safe for glass with privacy film?
faqs.a: Use non-ammonia, non-abrasive glass cleaner and soft microfiber; ammonia and razor scrapers can cloud or lift films. Green Seal GS-37 or ECOLOGO-certified glass cleaners meet most green cleaning policies, and SDS sheets must be on file under OSHA HazCom.

faqs.q: How often should glass partitions get a full detail clean?
faqs.a: Monthly works for most offices with high-visibility conference rooms; quarterly suits low-traffic internal glass. Client-facing lobbies and boardrooms may justify weekly detail. Touch-height spot cleaning should match your routine service frequency.
